This curriculum teaches you enough to ask the right question and catch a wrong answer. It is
not exam prep. If you want to go deeper, or want a credential that other people recognize,
this page lists the certifications that overlap with it and the best places to study.

Links checked and loading on 2026-11-11. Several sites (ASQ, HIMSS, ASCP, HIPAA Journal, HHS)
block automated checks, so they are named below without a link. Search for them by name. Many of
the study links are commercial or community content, not official sources. They are good for
learning, and they are never the authority for a regulatory claim. For that, go back to the
lessons and their sources.

## Certifications that map to this curriculum

Honest framing: most of these are built for people who do security, audit or quality work every
day. A Director of IT Service Operations is a strong candidate for a few of them and a stretch
for others. Requirements and prices change, so confirm them on the issuer's page before you plan
around one.

### ISC2 CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional)

- **Issuer:** [ISC2](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/cissp).
- **What it is:** a broad, management-level security certification. It tests judgment ("what
  would a security manager do first?") more than hands-on technical skill.
- **Eight domains:** (1) Security and Risk Management, (2) Asset Security, (3) Security
  Architecture and Engineering, (4) Communication and Network Security, (5) Identity and Access
  Management, (6) Security Assessment and Testing, (7) Security Operations, (8) Software
  Development Security.
- **Experience:** ISC2's
  [experience requirements page](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/cissp/cissp-experience-requirements)
  says candidates need a minimum of five years of cumulative, full-time experience in two or more
  of the eight domains, with some credit for a relevant degree or certain other credentials. It
  also says a candidate without the experience can pass the exam and become an Associate of ISC2,
  then has six years to earn the experience. Check the page for the current wording.
- **Heads-up:** ISC2's CISSP page says that effective April 15, 2027 the exam will be based on a
  new exam outline. Study from the outline that matches your exam date.
- **Overlap here:** [GRC frameworks and risk management](courses/grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/index.qmd),
  [Healthcare security and privacy](courses/healthcare-security-and-privacy/index.qmd), and
  [Vendor and third-party risk](courses/vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/index.qmd).
- **Realistic for you?** Plausible. Years of running IT operations, access, change and incident
  management likely touch at least two domains, but whether your history counts is ISC2's
  call. It is the best-known credential in the field and the one to use for the study material
  below. It is a lot of study for a credential the job does not require.

### ISC2 HCISPP (HealthCare Information Security and Privacy Practitioner)

- **Issuer:** [ISC2](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/hcispp).
- **What it is:** security and privacy specifically for healthcare. ISC2 lists seven domains:
  Healthcare Industry; Information Governance in Healthcare; Information Technologies in
  Healthcare; Regulatory and Standards Environment; Privacy and Security in Healthcare; Risk
  Management and Risk Assessment; and Third-Party Risk Management.
- **Experience:** ISC2's page lists two years of required work experience. Confirm the details
  there.
- **Overlap here:** this curriculum borrows its structure from the same body of knowledge. See
  [Healthcare security and privacy](courses/healthcare-security-and-privacy/index.qmd),
  [GRC frameworks and risk management](courses/grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/index.qmd) and
  [Vendor and third-party risk](courses/vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/index.qmd).
- **Realistic for you?** The closest fit by subject, and the lighter experience bar. A good first
  target if you want a credential that signals healthcare, not generic IT.

### ISC2 CC (Certified in Cybersecurity)

- **Issuer:** [ISC2](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/cc). Entry-level, no work experience
  required, five domains (security principles, governance, identity and access, network and
  cloud, operations and incident response).
- **Free?** It used to be free through ISC2's One Million Certified in Cybersecurity program. ISC2's
  [program page](https://www.isc2.org/landing/1mcc) now says the program has hit its goal and
  stopped new enrollments. Check ISC2 for current cost.
- **Realistic for you?** Probably below your level. Useful only as a cheap way to test whether you
  like exam-style study, or as a credential for a team member.

### ISACA CISA and CRISC

- **Issuer:** ISACA. [CISA](https://www.isaca.org/credentialing/cisa) (Certified Information Systems
  Auditor) is for IT audit and control. [CRISC](https://www.isaca.org/credentialing/crisc)
  (Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control) is for IT risk management.
- **Overlap here:** CRISC lines up with
  [GRC frameworks and risk management](courses/grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/index.qmd).
  CISA lines up with
  [Designing an internal audit program](courses/fda-and-aabb-in-practice/designing-an-internal-audit-program/index.qmd)
  and the [vendor risk course](courses/vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/index.qmd).
- **Experience:** both have experience requirements. The ISACA pages describe them, so check the
  current rules there.
- **Realistic for you?** CRISC is a natural fit for someone who reports risk to executives. CISA
  fits if you want to audit IT yourself, which is closer to the Quality Analyst's role than yours.

### ASQ CQA and CMQ/OE

- **Issuer:** ASQ (American Society for Quality). Its site blocked automated checks, so no link
  here. Search "ASQ Certified Quality Auditor" and "ASQ Manager of Quality/Organizational
  Excellence".
- **What they are:** CQA (Certified Quality Auditor) is the standard credential for quality
  auditing. CMQ/OE is aimed at quality managers and leaders.
- **Overlap here:** [Quality system essentials](courses/quality-system-essentials/index.qmd),
  [Designing an internal audit program](courses/fda-and-aabb-in-practice/designing-an-internal-audit-program/index.qmd)
  and [Directing the Quality Analyst](courses/directing-the-quality-analyst/index.qmd).
- **Realistic for you?** The CQA is a better goal for your Quality Analyst than for you. The
  CMQ/OE is a stretch worth considering if you want the quality vocabulary in depth. Check ASQ's
  current requirements.

### AHIMA CHPS

- **Issuer:** [AHIMA](https://www.ahima.org/certification-careers/certifications-overview/chps/)
  (health information management). CHPS is Certified in Healthcare Privacy and Security.
- **Experience:** AHIMA's page lists several routes that combine education with years of
  healthcare privacy or security experience (for example, a bachelor's degree plus two years). Read
  the page for the route that fits you.
- **Overlap here:** [Healthcare security and privacy](courses/healthcare-security-and-privacy/index.qmd)
  and [Data integrity and records](courses/data-integrity-and-records/index.qmd).
- **Realistic for you?** Only if your role includes real privacy or security duties. It leans
  toward health-records people more than IT operations.

### HIMSS CPHIMS

- **Issuer:** HIMSS (health information and management systems). Its site blocked automated
  checks, so no link here. Search "HIMSS CPHIMS".
- **What it is:** a professional credential for health IT and information management.
- **Overlap here:** the [ITSM bridge course](courses/itsm-for-regulated-blood-services/index.qmd)
  and general health IT context. Check HIMSS for current requirements.
- **Realistic for you?** Fits a healthcare IT career path, but little of the exam is
  blood-center specific. Lower priority.

### ITIL 4 (PeopleCert)

- **Issuer:** PeopleCert runs the ITIL exams. The framework is published by
  [AXELOS](https://www.axelos.com/).
- **Overlap here:** this is the vocabulary you already use, and the
  [ITSM for regulated blood services](courses/itsm-for-regulated-blood-services/index.qmd) capstone
  translates it into quality-system language.
- **Realistic for you?** You probably know the content. Take a higher ITIL level only if it helps
  your career. The more useful move is the crosswalk in that course.

### ASCP SBB (Specialist in Blood Banking)

- **Issuer:** ASCP Board of Certification. Its site blocked automated checks, so no link here.
  Search "ASCP Specialist in Blood Banking SBB".
- **What it is:** an advanced technical credential held by blood bank specialists. It is not a goal
  for you. It is useful context for what the blood bank's own experts have studied, and
  for how to talk to them.
- **Overlap here:** [Blood center operations](courses/blood-center-operations/index.qmd).

## CISSP domains and where this curriculum touches them

This is a map, not an equivalence. The curriculum covers regulated blood-center systems, not
exam prep. Some domains, especially network and software development security, are barely
touched here, so use the study links to fill them.

| CISSP domain | Where this curriculum touches it | One good free study link |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Security and Risk Management | [Risk frameworks side by side](courses/grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/risk-frameworks-side-by-side/index.qmd), [Quality risk management](courses/quality-system-essentials/quality-risk-management/index.qmd), [The HIPAA Privacy Rule](courses/healthcare-security-and-privacy/the-hipaa-privacy-rule/index.qmd) | [Destination Certification: Align Security Function to Business Strategy](https://destcert.com/resources/alignment-of-security-function-to-business-strategy-mindmap-cissp-domain-1/) (commercial company, free page) |
| 2. Asset Security | [Retention across record types](courses/data-integrity-and-records/retention-across-record-types/index.qmd), [ALCOA and data integrity](courses/data-integrity-and-records/alcoa-and-data-integrity/index.qmd), [Information governance in a covered entity](courses/healthcare-security-and-privacy/information-governance-in-a-covered-entity/index.qmd) | [Destination Certification CISSP mindmaps](https://destcert.com/cissp-mindmaps/) (commercial) |
| 3. Security Architecture and Engineering | [GAMP 5 and the V-model](courses/csv-and-becs/gamp5-and-the-v-model/index.qmd), [BECS as a regulated device](courses/csv-and-becs/becs-as-a-regulated-device/index.qmd) | [SANS posters and cheat sheets](https://www.sans.org/posters/) |
| 4. Communication and Network Security | Light touch: [BECS interfaces and data integrity](courses/csv-and-becs/becs-interfaces-and-data-integrity/index.qmd) | [SANS security resources](https://www.sans.org/security-resources/) |
| 5. Identity and Access Management | [Audit trails and e-signatures](courses/data-integrity-and-records/audit-trails-and-esignatures/index.qmd), [Security Rule safeguards and Part 11](courses/healthcare-security-and-privacy/security-rule-safeguards-and-part-11/index.qmd) | [Mike Chapple on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@CertMike) (security certification lessons) |
| 6. Security Assessment and Testing | [Implement and assess controls](courses/grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/implement-and-assess-controls/index.qmd), [IQ, OQ, PQ and traceability](courses/csv-and-becs/iq-oq-pq-and-traceability/index.qmd), [Internal audits and management review](courses/quality-system-essentials/internal-audits-and-management-review/index.qmd) | [NIST Risk Management Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf) |

Software Development Security | Light touch: [Vendor change notifications](courses/vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/vendor-change-notifications-and-your-own-change-control/index.qmd), [QMSR, ISO 13485 and the vendor](courses/csv-and-becs/qmsr-iso-13485-and-the-vendor/index.qmd) | [ISC2 CISSP exam outline](https://www.isc2.org/Certifications/CISSP/CISSP-Certification-Exam-Outline) (official, lists what is tested) |

## Free study material

- [ISC2 CISSP exam outline](https://www.isc2.org/Certifications/CISSP/CISSP-Certification-Exam-Outline).
  Official. Start here: it says exactly what is tested.
- [Destination Certification CISSP mindmaps](https://destcert.com/cissp-mindmaps/). Commercial
  training company. The free mind maps give you the shape of each domain before you dig in.
- [Kelly Handerhan at Destination Certification](https://destcert.com/kelly-handerhan/). Commercial.
  A well-known CISSP instructor, and the page for her courses. Her advice to "think like a
  manager" suits your role.
- [Cybrary Podcast episode 69: A Humanizing Approach to Passing the CISSP Exam with Kelly Handerhan](https://www.cybrary.it/podcast/a-humanizing-approach-to-passing-the-cissp-exam-with-kelly-handerhan-the-cybrary-podcast-ep-69).
  A listen-on-the-commute introduction to the exam mindset.
- [Inside Cloud and Security on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@InsideCloudAndSecurity). Commercial
  channel with long CISSP exam-cram videos that cover every domain. Check that the video you pick
  matches the current exam outline.
- [Mike Chapple on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@CertMike) and
  [CertMike](https://certmike.com/). Commercial. Security educator with
  free study groups and plain-English explanations (per the site).
- [SANS posters and cheat sheets](https://www.sans.org/posters/). SANS is a commercial training
  institute, but the posters are free, and good one-page references.
- [SANS security resources](https://www.sans.org/security-resources/). Free reading, tools
  and reference material.
- [ISACA Journal](https://www.isaca.org/resources/isaca-journal). Practitioner articles on
  governance, risk and audit. Some content is for members only.
- [ISPE Pharmaceutical Engineering](https://www.ispe.org/pharmaceutical-engineering). Magazine from
  the society behind GAMP. Useful for validation and data integrity in regulated manufacturing.
- [itsm.tools](https://itsm.tools/). Commercial ITSM blog and tool reviews. Good for ITSM practice
  and tooling context, not for regulation.
- [NIST Risk Management Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf).
  Public, free, and the backbone of the
  [GRC course](courses/grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/index.qmd).
- [NIST Cybersecurity Framework](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework). A plain-language control
  vocabulary used across many industries.
- [ISC2 Insights blog](https://www.isc2.org/Insights). Free reading from the CISSP issuer.

## Podcasts and newsletters

- [Blood Bank Guy Essentials Podcast](https://www.bbguy.org/). Interviews on transfusion medicine
  with Joe Chaffin, MD. AABB also lists it on its [podcast page](https://www.aabb.org/bbguy).
  Aimed at clinicians, but the best free way to hear how blood bank experts talk.
- [Risky Business](https://risky.biz/netcasts/risky-business/). Security news podcast.
- [Darknet Diaries](https://darknetdiaries.com/). Storytelling about real incidents. Good for
  seeing how breaches unfold, and for your incident-response instincts.
- [SANS NewsBites](https://www.sans.org/newsletters/newsbites/). Security news digest
  with expert commentary.
- [SANS OUCH! newsletter](https://www.sans.org/newsletters/ouch/). Plain-language security
  awareness newsletter. Useful to forward to staff.
- [ISACA newsletters](https://www.isaca.org/resources/news-and-trends/newsletters). Governance,
  risk and audit news from the issuer of CISA and CRISC.
